predecessors.name: Imagawa clan
predecessors.text: Kaminogō and the Okazaki area of Mikawa

successors.name: Tokugawa shogunate
successors.text: the five Hōjō provinces 'Sagami, Izu, Musashi, Shimosa, and Kazusa', given to Ieyasu in 1590

ledger.x: 1561: 'he openly ended his allegiance to the Imagawa clan and captured Kaminogō castle.'
By 1565: 'Ieyasu had become the master of all of Mikawa Province'.
1568-1569: 'Ieyasu besieged the Horikawa Castle in Tōtōmi' in 1568 and captured it in 1569; 1570 Hamamatsu is the capital.
1572: Shingen's move against Futamata and Hamamatsu; 'Shingen later captured Tokugawa's Futamata Castle'.
1574: Katsuyori 'captured Takatenjin castle, which even his father had not managed to do'.

1581: Ieyasu 'recapture[d] Takatenjin castle' after building fortresses to isolate it in 1580; Katsuyori 'lost Takatenjin fortress to Tokugawa Ieyasu, and 680 men of Okabe Motonobu's garrison died in the siege'.
1581: the Tōtōmi front closes with the loss of Takatenjin; the page gives no peace.
1582: 'Nobunaga gave Ieyasu the right to govern Suruga Province' after the Takeda collapse.
1582: the Tenshō-Jingo war; 'Tokugawa Ieyasu gained much of Kai Province and Shinano Province'.
1590: 'relocated to the Kanto plains' under Toyotomi.
1600: 'After Hideyoshi's death and the Battle of Sekigahara, Ieyasu seized power in 1600'; the Sengoku page: the Eastern Army under Ieyasu defeated the Western Army.

wars.name: Battle of Mikatagahara
wars.outcome: Takeda victory on 25 January 1573 north of Hamamatsu; the Tokugawa-Oda force 'almost totally annihilated'; Shingen withdrew and died in May 1573.

wars.name: Battle of Nagashino
wars.outcome: The Oda-Tokugawa force (38,000) won a great victory over Katsuyori; no land changed at once.

wars.name: Siege of Takatenjin
wars.outcome: Ieyasu built fortresses to isolate the castle in 1580 and recaptured it in 1581.

wars.name: Tenshō-Jingo War
wars.outcome: A triangular conflict over Shinano, Kōzuke and Kai; Ieyasu gained much of Kai and Shinano.

wars.name: Battle of Komaki and Nagakute
wars.outcome: Inconclusive against Hideyoshi; no territory change on the pages.

wars.name: Sekigahara campaign
wars.outcome: The Eastern Army under Ieyasu defeated the Western Army of Toyotomi loyalists; Ieyasu seized power in 1600.

certainty.note: The pages name castles and provinces, not borders; the Mikawa, Tōtōmi, Suruga, Kai and Shinano shapes are circles and prefectures.
